aria: Animated recap of the Thunder's 126 to 120 home win over the Pelicans: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's step-back 3-pointer with 3:16 left that made it 114 to 110, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Gilgeous-Alexander's 40 points, the top scorers, how the Thunder won, and Sunday's game at the Heat.

notes: Box score from the Oklahoma City Thunder's 126–120 home win over the New Orleans Pelicans on Nov 20, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, checked against the Plain Text Sports game page, with game details from the Associated Press (via News9), Field Level Media (via Yardbarker), OKC Thunder Wire (via Yahoo Sports) and Crescent City Sports. All 126 Oklahoma City points and all 120 New Orleans points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores (33–23–36–34 to 36–28–34–22) add up to both totals: 64–56 New Orleans at the half and 98–92 New Orleans after three (AP). Team totals (field goals 49 of 92 to 42 of 93, threes 14 of 36 to 17 of 39, assists 26–23) are from the box score; points in the paint (60–42) and the biggest leads (Oklahoma City 11, New Orleans 16) are from Plain Text Sports and Covers.com, which agree. First-half and fourth-quarter points are from the line score. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Friday's games.

Oklahoma City opened the game 11–0, and New Orleans led for most of the next three quarters (Plain Text Sports play-by-play); the Pelicans' biggest lead was 94–78 on Trey Murphy III's 3-pointer with 3:37 left in the third. The Thunder closed the third on a 16–7 run (AP), Jared McCain's 24-footer tied it at 102 with 9:22 left (AP), and Ajay Mitchell's driving floater at 8:52 put Oklahoma City ahead 104–102 for good (Plain Text Sports). Saddiq Bey's three-point play cut it to 111–110 with 3:31 left before Gilgeous-Alexander's step-back three made it 114–110 (Plain Text Sports; Field Level Media). His three-point play with 34.8 seconds left made it 124–116 (AP). Gilgeous-Alexander had 40 points on 14-of-24 shooting with 8 assists, 19 of them by halftime (AP); it was his fourth 40-point game of the season (Field Level Media). Aday Mara had career highs of 22 points and 16 rebounds, and Bennett Stirtz a career-high 18 off the bench (Field Level Media). The Thunder are 2–1 in NBA Cup group play and 8–5 since losing three starters to long-term injuries (AP). Oklahoma City plays at Miami on Sunday and New Orleans at San Antonio on Saturday (Plain Text Sports schedule).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 26-foot step-back 3-pointer with 3:16 left in the fourth quarter that made it 114–110 (Plain Text Sports play-by-play gives the clock, distance, shot type and score; Field Level Media and Crescent City Sports say it came over Zion Williamson). The step-back move itself is not drawn: it uses the template's plain pull-up three. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Oklahoma City Thunder or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's listed 6-foot-6 and 195 pounds with No. 2 and a reported 6-foot-11 wingspan (Wikipedia; Basketball-Reference). He is drawn in Oklahoma City's home white with his look from the look sheet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
